title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 116 (Resolutions passed at adjourned meeting)

content.overview: Where a resolution is passed at an adjourned meeting of a company, or of holders of any class of shares, or of the Board of Directors, the resolution shall for all purposes be treated as having been passed on the date on which it was in fact passed, and shall not be deemed to have been passed on any earlier date.
content.glance: A resolution passed at an adjourned meeting is treated as passed on its actual date, not an earlier date.
content.study:
## Section 116 — Resolutions passed at adjourned meeting

Section 116 covers an adjourned meeting of a company, holders of a class of shares, or the Board. The resolution is treated as passed on the date it was in fact passed — not backdated to the original meeting.

The actual passing date may determine when a connected filing period under section 117 begins. Section 116 is a date rule only; it does not validate a resolution that lacked notice, quorum, authority or the required majority.

**Example.** A meeting is adjourned on 10 June without passing a resolution. The resolution is passed at the adjourned meeting on 24 June. Section 116 treats 24 June as the date of passage.

This note is a focused study aid; the topic remains under source and current-law review.

hypotheticals.question: Does section 116 cure a resolution that lacked the required majority at the adjourned meeting?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 116 is only a date-of-passage rule. It does not cure defects in notice, quorum, authority or voting.

misconceptions.correction: The resolution is treated as passed on the date it was in fact passed.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What is the effect of section 116?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: A resolution passed at an adjourned meeting of a company, class of shareholders, or the Board is treated as passed on the date it was actually passed, not an earlier date. It does not cure independent validity defects.
